fr.elements: Main Building; Front Driveway; Access Road; Open Green Space; Landscaped Area; Dense Vegetation; Perimeter Fencing; Street Frontage; Open Terrain; Pedestrian Walkways
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Long Driveway; Dense Vegetation; Open Terrain; Limited Rear Access
fr.recommendations: Ensuring that the single driveway entry point is clearly marked and visible from the access road could improve initial response times and navigation for arriving units. Given the length of the driveway, designating a staging area near the front of the property may assist apparatus positioning and support coordination between multiple responding units. Trimming or managing dense vegetation along the driveway corridor could enhance visibility and maneuvering clearance for larger emergency vehicles. Addressing limited rear access by identifying or maintaining any available pedestrian walkways as secondary movement routes for personnel may support ground-level operations around the structure.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Shrubs; Heavy Brush; Scattered Shrubs; Brush Concentration; Mixed Vegetation Cover; Vegetation Adjacent to Structure; Limited Defensible Space; Fuel Continuity; Open Terrain; Single Access Route; Brushland Interface; Scattered Trees
wildfire.recommendations: Reducing the density of heavy brush and concentrated brush areas on the property, particularly within the immediate vicinity of the structure, could meaningfully improve defensible space and reduce fuel continuity across the site. Where shrubs and mixed vegetation are growing adjacent to or in close proximity to the structure, increasing horizontal separation between individual plants and between vegetation and the structure would support suppression operations and reduce direct fuel exposure to the building. Managing vegetation to create irregular spacing rather than continuous cover may reduce the opportunity for fire to travel uninterrupted across the property. Given that access to the property relies on a single route through a brushland interface, maintaining that access road clear of encroaching shrubs and overhanging vegetation along its full length is a practical priority, as it would support both evacuation and firefighter access. Preserving any existing open terrain on the property as a natural fuel break, and avoiding future introduction of additional vegetation in those areas, could further support long-term wildfire resilience.
